yangon.title: Myanmar: Is the US undermining the EU’s diplomatic blockade?
detail: With the US reopening talks with Myanmar's military-backed government, and several Southeast Asian countries restarting diplomatic contacts, the EU is facing uncomfortable questions about its own boycott of the junta. (DW)

The US government has begun a quiet reproachment with Myanmar’s military-backed government, holding two rounds of talks since September with State Department representative Michael Vance. American diplomats reportedly meet Myanmar officials in Naypyitaw and then in Tokyo earlier this month. (Inquirer)

yangon.title: Hong Kong beautician gets 4 years for selling friends to Myanmar scam hub
detail: A Hong Kong beautician has been sentenced to four years in jail for tricking two friends into forced labour and confinement in Myanmar’s notorious “KK Park” scam farm, with a judge slamming her actions as “vicious and inhumane”. (South China Morning Post)

yangon.title: Myanmar refugee in Denmark demands justice over junta war crimes
detail: A Myanmar citizen living in Denmark on Monday filed a complaint with Danish authorities against the country’s ruling military junta for alleged war crimes committed against minorities. (South China Morning Post)

yangon.title: How purchases of sanctioned Iranian jet fuel were disguised by Myanmar
detail: The lengths taken to disguise the trade suggest U.S. sanctions are biting, but Iranian jet fuel has continued to flow. (The Japan Times)

yangon.title: After nearly 6 years, ex-Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi's son hears her voice
detail: Kim Aris says ‘hearing her voice again means more than words can express’ amid loosening of detention restrictions The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi has been allowed to speak to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years. (The Guardian)

The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi said she sounded “fairly healthy” after speaking to the detained ex-democratic leader on Thursday for the first time in more than five years. (South China Morning Post)

yangon.title: Filipinos on the line: Inside a Myanmar scam operation
detail: MAE SOT, Thailand — She starts work at 4 p.m., using her company-issued iPhone 14. Assigned to Line 1, she randomly dials phone numbers belonging to people more than 8,000 miles away. Denise (not her real name) sighs when someone answers. On the other end is an elderly American man, probably sitting on a couch (Inquirer)

pyongyang.title: Why Kim Jong-un’s border trip to China differs from past pre-summit playbooks
detail: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday echoed the intense coordination that preceded his previous summits with US President Donald Trump. (South China Morning Post)

pyongyang.title: North Korean howitzer guns spotted close to border with South Korea
detail: The presence of the self-propelled 122-mm howitzer near the border marks a rare visible deployment of such artillery. (The Japan Times)
North Korean howitzer guns have been seen close to the border with South Korea - at a time when tensions between the two nations are high. (Sky News)

pyongyang.title: North Korea tells UN South ‘fabricated’ border landmine blast
detail: North Korea sent a letter to the United Nations Security Council accusing Seoul of fabricating a landmine explosion that injured three South Korean soldiers, its state media reported Monday. (South China Morning Post)
South Korea blames Pyongyang for September landmine blast, but North Korea says incident a 'sinister obstructive move'. (Al Jazeera)

pyongyang.title: ‘Call of Duty’ North Korea invasion edition tops sales charts in South
detail: SEOUL — The latest installment of the “Call of Duty” video game franchise, featuring a full-scale North Korean invasion of South Korea, has topped sales charts in the would-be target, even as real-life border tensions are ratcheting higher. (Inquirer)

South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung has been urged by critics to play the latest instalment in the blockbuster Call of Duty video game franchise to better appreciate the need for defences against an invasion by the North. (South China Morning Post)

pyongyang.title: Kim Jong-un ‘dead’ again: Why rumors about N. Korean leaders never die
detail: Rumors that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un died after suffering a brain hemorrhage have swept through social media and news outlets overseas in recent days, prompting South Korean officials to dismiss the claims as unsubstantiated, while Pyongyang released fresh photographs of its leader attending a public event. (Inquirer)

pyongyang.title: N. Korea has planted nearly 1 million land mines in DMZ – Seoul
detail: North Korea has planted an estimated 960,000 land mines in the Demilitarized Zone since 2024 as part of a campaign to fortify its border with South Korea, according to military data disclosed Friday. (Inquirer)

pyongyang.title: North Korea’s Kim visits China as allies look to boost economic ties
detail: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was accompanied during his visit to the border city of Dandong on Saturday by Wang Huning, China's No. 4 official. (The Japan Times)

pyongyang.title: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un arrives in Chinese border city
detail: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un arrived in the Chinese city of Dandong, his second visit in just over a year and before US President Donald Trump travels to the region next month. (Bloomberg)
South Korean officials say Kim arrived in Dandong using the New Yalu River Bridge, which opened about a week ago. (Al Jazeera)

singapore.title: Singapore court fines behavioural therapist for hurting autistic boy who hit her
detail: A Singaporean behavioural therapist who was repeatedly hit in the face by a four-year-old boy with special needs grabbed his hand and dragged him off his chair and onto the floor. Tricia Lee Hsien, 29, was fined S$5,000 (US$3,900) by a court on Wednesday. (South China Morning Post)

singapore.title: Prabowo to Meet Singapore Envoy on Mission to Ease Relations
detail: Indonesia President Prabowo Subianto will meet Singapore’s top diplomat on Wednesday as ties between the two Southeast Asian nations come under strain. (Bloomberg)

singapore.title: Why Singapore’s PAP internal vote is the wrong place to look for signs of leadership renewal
detail: Singapore’s ruling People’s Action Party (PAP) has retained its core executive team in what is seen as a cautious approach despite pledges of renewal, with observers pointing to ministerial promotions as a better indication of leadership plans. (South China Morning Post)

singapore.title: Singapore, Indonesia to create haze task force, share data amid tensions
detail: Indonesia and Singapore are looking to set up a joint task force to deal with haze from Indonesia’s wildfires, the countries’ foreign ministers said on Tuesday, as they met to reaffirm their ties after weeks of simmering tensions. (South China Morning Post)

singapore.title: Singaporean woman admits to conspiring to abuse Megan Khung, helping dispose of her body
detail: A Singaporean woman pleaded guilty on Monday to conspiring with a friend and the friend’s boyfriend to abuse four-year-old Megan Khung, and helping to dispose of the child’s body after she died following months of abuse. (South China Morning Post)

singapore.title: Singapore’s Top Envoy Visits Indonesia After Natural Gas Cuts
detail: Indonesia has defended its decision to cut natural gas exports to Singapore, citing domestic electricity and industrial needs and arguing that the reduction remains within contractual limits. (South China Morning Post)
Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan is scheduled to meet his Indonesian counterpart in Jakarta on Tuesday, days after Indonesia trimmed natural gas exports to the city-state. (Bloomberg)

singapore.title: Singapore’s toxic haze probe expands to 10 palm oil, forestry firms
detail: Singapore has expanded its investigation into haze-creating fires in Indonesia that have blanketed the city state in smog, requesting information from 10 locally registered companies. (South China Morning Post)

singapore.title: Singapore tells suppliers to ‘honour commitments’ amid Indonesia’s gas cut
detail: Singapore expects all parties who have signed commercial contracts for gas supplies to “honour their commitments”, said Prime Minister Lawrence Wong on Sunday after Indonesia cut its exports. (South China Morning Post)

wellington.title: Abhishek Sharma hits ton as India beat New Zealand by 6 wickets in 3rd T20
detail: The opening pair put on 133-run partnership as India chased down 199 to wrap up the five-match T20 series. (Al Jazeera)

wellington.title: Former New Zealand PM Ardern to mentor students in new Australian gig
detail: Former New Zealand prime minister will focus on leadership, social cohesion and public health in new role The former New Zealand prime minister Jacinda Ardern will lecture and mentor at the University of Sydney after moving to Australia earlier this year. (The Guardian)

SYDNEY — Former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern has taken up a post at a major Australian university. Ms Ardern, who was her home country’s leader from 2017 to 2023, will soon begin guest-lecturing, running masterclasses and mentoring students and researchers at the University of Sydney. (Inquirer)

wellington.title: India resist New Zealand fightback to win record-setting T20 cricket opener
detail: New Zealand reach their highest home total against India, 225-4, but Sanju Samson hits fifty to top the record in chase. (Al Jazeera)

wellington.title: CII urges exporters, MSMEs to tap opportunities under India-New Zealand FTA
detail: CII's Sanjay Budhia said New Zealand can also serve as a gateway to the wider Oceania and Pacific Island markets. (The Hindu)

wellington.title: New Zealand Inflation Slows Ahead of Year-End Fuel Spike
detail: New Zealand’s annual inflation slowed more than expected in the third quarter as fuel prices retreated, offering a brief respite to the government little more than two weeks from an election. (Bloomberg)

kathmandu.title: Nepali worker’s death in Saudi Arabia leaves family deep in debt
detail: On Monday evening, the courtyard of a home at Dhekaha in ward 1 of Pipara Rural Municipality, Mahottari, was crowded with neighbours. A pall of grief hung over the gathering. Sitting quietly and struggling to steady herself was 41-year-old Indrika Devi Mahato. (Inquirer)

kathmandu.title: [OPINION] Twilight time for the CPP-NPA’s forever war
detail: The communist party could take the cue from the its counterparts in Nepal, who signed a peace agreement with the Nepalese government in 2006 and became the ruling party through democratic elections in 2008–2009 and has been in the ruling coalition several times since then (Rappler)

kathmandu.title: Devoid of options, Nepal flood survivors return to damaged homes
detail: Ram Kumar Bhandari and his seven-member family have returned, after two months, to the same house that was buried by mud and debris in the August 26 Bhotekoshi flood. Their safety there remains uncertain. After the disaster, Bhandari rented a house in Pipaltar for about a month. (Inquirer)

kathmandu.title: Bay of Bengal cyclone to bring rain, snow to Nepal from Thursday night
detail: A low-pressure system developing over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a powerful cyclone, bringing cloudy skies to Nepal from Wednesday and increasing the likelihood of rain from Thursday, according to the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology. (Inquirer)

kathmandu.title: Nepal-based gang arrested in retired IPS officer’s wife murder case after six-month hunt
detail: Police also said the gang members had planned similar offences in Bengaluru and Delhi by employing domestic servants and that their arrest prevented the commission of those offences. (The Hindu)

kathmandu.title: Two Japanese climbers die on remote Himalayan peak in Nepal
detail: The climbers were attempting the first summit of the 7,140-meter Gangapurna West in alpine style, but lost contact after Oct. 15. (The Japan Times)

kathmandu.title: Nepal set to receive first-ever US$20 million payout from UN climate damage fund
detail: The United Nations’ climate loss and damage fund moved to provide US$20 million in aid sought by flood-stricken Nepal – the first time it has set aside money for any country – in a key test of the body’s credibility. (South China Morning Post)

kathmandu.title: Nepal wants to test whether COP31 can deliver climate justice
detail: KATHMANDU — Nepal has made an emergency appeal to the UN’s loss-and-damage fund, which has yet to disburse any money. nuuk.title: Why China’s new estimate on Greenland ice loss speed is 55% lower than America’s
detail: Chinese researchers have created a new model to convert satellite surface elevation data for the Greenland Ice Sheet into a detailed estimate of how much ice it has lost in recent decades. (South China Morning Post)
